readings_ruling: « induisant φ sur P » (absent from the affine 1°, l.631–632; the scan, journal p. 256, PDF p. 29 rendered at 110 dpi, agrees with the transcription word for word). The text settles it, so it is a misprint-level omission and needs no OQ of its own. (1) The forward reference states the extension for the affine case in so many words: « φ se prolonge en une application projective (resp. affine) de V sur S(n) (resp. ℝⁿ) » (l.184–185; scan p. 248, PDF p. 21, checked). (2) The proof is « comme le précédent » (l.644–645), and the projective 1° prints « induisant φ sur P » (l.522–523). Its a builds φ̃ « coïncidant avec φ sur P » (l.538–539). (3) The reading taken is the STRONGER statement. Every Lean statement carries EqOn φ̃ φ P, and the literal form follows (PremierAffinePrinted.literal), so the choice cannot make Lean < paper. This is the same footing as the Remark's « connexe » in T-bz-c2-cas-affin. The REPORT's justification, « the second sentence needs it », overstates. The literal sentence is well formed: z is a function on ℝⁿ and φ̃ maps into ℝⁿ, and PremierAffineLiteralPrinted states that sentence. What needs EqOn is the intended meaning, namely that {z < 1} is the pocket's half-space in φ's coordinates. The REPORT never cites l.184–185, which is the decisive evidence. One corner remains, and it belongs inside OQ-71, not in a new OQ. Suppose OQ-71 demands the full form and the EqOn full form were refuted for some n ≥ 2. Then the literal full form (some other half-space g⁻¹{z < 1}) would be a distinct and weaker fallback. The master can mention this when extending OQ-71 to this row.

labels.label: bzthm:c2s3t2_poche_balayable_affine
labels.notes: Only 1° is in scope (2°–4° belong to T-bz-c2-theoreme-affine). The label is unmarked, as dispatched. It appears as `bzthm:…` at l.11, within the first 4000 characters, and no ``**`bz`` occurs anywhere in the file. Statement checked against l.627–646 and the scan p. 256. Hypotheses: « variété localement affine connexe balayable » becomes [ChartedSpace (Fin n → ℝ) V] [HasGroupoid V (affGroupoid n)] [PreconnectedSpace V] plus IsBalayable (GAR n) (Fin n → ℝ) V (Déf. 15 for the whole automorphism group, as printed). « (P, φ, z) une poche » is IsPocheAff (strict Déf. 1). Every n, n = 0 included. These assume no more than the paper (no T2, no second countability), so Lean ≥ paper. First sentence: exists_chart_poche_affine and theoreme_premier_affine give an OpenPartialHomeomorph (open target) with IsCompatibleChart (GAR n), source = univ, and EqOn φ̃ φ P. That is the print plus « induisant φ sur P », the stronger form (readings_ruling). The chart is unique as a map (IsDeveloping.eq_of_eqOn_poche_affine, which needs only hP). Second sentence: the component form (poche_eq_connectedComponentIn_affine), plus the iff with preconnectedness of {z < 1} ∩ φ̃(V). The full form is weaker than the print, which is disclosed, and the row is partial and unmarked. Printed forms. PremierAffinePrinted (l.607–614) is exactly the printed 1° under the EqOn reading. It quantifies over T2, connected, second-countable V : Type with an affine structure, IsBalayable, and IsPocheAff, and concludes P = φ̃⁻¹({z < 1} ∩ range φ̃), the same set as φ̃⁻¹{z < 1}. It matches the projective PremierPrinted binder for binder. PremierAffineLiteralPrinted (l.619–626) is the literal print, with no EqOn, and PremierAffinePrinted.literal really derives it by dropping the conjunct. ConnexeAffinePrinted (l.632–639) quantifies over every chart with EqOn, which is harmless because the chart exists and is unique. premierAffinePrinted_iff (l.649–660) does not hold by unfolding. An audit probe showed that `Iff.rfl` fails. The proof goes through uniqueness, the open embedding (injectivity of every developing map), and the component form (closure step, condition b). Generic (G, X) lemmas (namespace PremierGX). Their hypotheses are a compatible chart with source P, IsConnected P, hmove (every compact set moved into P by an automorphism), PreconnectedSpace, LocPathConnectedSpace, and IsAnalyticAction G X. All of them are discharged at GA(n): IsPocheAff gives the chart, Prop. 7′ with G := ⊤ gives hmove (compact_dans_poche_affine), and the strict files supply locPathConnectedSpace_of_aff and instIsAnalyticActionGAR. Both witnesses go through them, so the instantiation is neither vacuous nor wrong. « z ≡ 0 is the only constant cote » is true. If z is constant, its infimum on the nonempty φ(P) is that constant, so condition a forces it to be 0 (IsPocheAff.cote_eq_zero_of_linear_eq_zero, from z.linear = 0). Under the paper's « fonction linéaire » read as homogeneous it is immediate. Under Lean's affine z it uses condition a. z ≡ 0 is a pocket: isPocheAff_model. The n ≤ 1 case is genuine. For n = 0 every set of Fin 0 → ℝ is convex. For n = 1, preconnected means convex through funUnique and Mathlib's IsPreconnected.convex (alias of Real.convex_iff_isPreconnected). range φ̃ is preconnected (V connected), so {z < 1} ∩ range φ̃ is convex. The star-shaped case is also correct. A nonempty StarConvex c (range p) contains c, and with z c < 1 the intersection is star-convex about c, hence path connected. The REPORT's argued cone case was checked by hand and is correct. If z(c) ≥ 1, the rays h_t(x), t ≥ 1, from x ∈ φ(P) stay in φ̃(V) ∩ {z < 1}, are joined to x by a segment, and so lie in P with z → −∞, against inf z = 0. If z(c) < 1, contracting a path of φ̃(V) towards c joins any two points inside {z < 1}.

oq_independence: The file is independent of OQ-61: nothing assumes a non-constant cote. Under OQ-61 (a), the ℝⁿ witness (z ≡ 0) would stop being a pocket, but the half-space witness, whose cote is non-constant, survives. non_vacuity: Both witnesses apply theoreme_premier_affine itself to hypotheses proved in strict files. theoreme_premier_affine_model covers ℝⁿ for every n, with IsBalayableFor translationSubgroup and IsBalayable, the pocket (univ, refl, 0), and P = V, full form included. theoreme_premier_affine_demiEspace covers the half-space {x₀ > 0} ⊂ ℝⁿ⁺¹ for every n, with isBalayable_demiEspaceOuvert and exists_isPocheAff_demiEspace. It states P = {x₀ < 1} ≠ univ (the point x ≡ 2) and ∃ y, z y ≠ 0 (z = proj 0 at the all-ones vector), so the cote is non-constant. It also proves the full form there, via the convexity of {0 < x₀ < 1}. The fix asked of the projective witness in T-bz-c2-developpement's audit is already applied here.
